reason: The digestive tube has a named slot for the salivary glands, which connect to the mouth.
expectation: The salivary glands will fit into the digestive tube.

effect: The salivary glands fit into the digestive tube as expected; the other named organ slots remain to be filled.
reason: The pancreas has a named slot and its duct leads to the small intestine.
expectation: The pancreas will fit into the digestive tube.

effect: The pancreas fitted as expected, leaving the liver and gallbladder as the remaining available glandular organs.
reason: The liver and gallbladder have a named slot, and their bile ducts lead toward the intestine.
expectation: The liver and gallbladder will fit into the digestive tube.

effect: The organ fittings completed the first goal and clarified what each contributes to digestion.
reaction: The brief explanation made the fittings more meaningful.
reason: Salivary amylase is shown beside starch chains, and saliva begins starch digestion.
expectation: The amylase will begin breaking down the starch.

effect: Salivary amylase shortened the starch chains; they may need further digestion before absorption.
reaction: The result makes the first stage of starch digestion clear.
reason: The remaining starch-digesting enzymes are described as acting in the small intestine.
expectation: The enzymes will break the chains into smaller sugars for absorption.

effect: The remaining enzymes broke the starch chains into individual glucose molecules that can cross the intestinal lining.
reaction: The two stages of starch digestion were clear.
reason: The protein-digesting enzymes are shown beside protein chains, so they are a likely match for the protein food.
expectation: The enzymes will break the protein into smaller components for absorption.

effect: Protein digestion produced individual amino acids; fat remains to be broken down.
reason: Bile and lipase are shown working on fat droplets, making them the clear match for fat food.
expectation: The fat will be broken down into components suitable for absorption.

effect: The fat became fatty acids and monoglycerides, completing the digestion goal. The explanation distinguished bile’s role in dispersing fat from lipase’s role in breaking it down.
reaction: That distinction was useful and more interesting than the straightforward pairing.

mostWorthwhile.text: Breaking down fat was most worthwhile because the result explained the different jobs of bile and lipase, including that bile is not an enzyme.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the first two organs felt repetitive: both were named slots, and their individual results added little explanation.

surprise.text: The fat result clarified that bile disperses fat into droplets while lipase breaks the molecules apart.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; the named slots and ingredient descriptions made the choices clear.

continue.text: I would be mildly interested in continuing to see how the digestion products cross the gut lining, although the mostly obvious pairings made this chapter feel more instructional than challenging.
